prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your specific case (single tooth vs full-arch, need for bone grafting/sinus lift), who you feel comfortable with, and the provider’s training and experience. I can help you find a great implant provider in Columbus, but first here are practical ways to identify the best fit:

What type of clinician to look for
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons — specialize in surgical placement of implants and complex bone/graft procedures. Often ABOMS board-certified.
- Periodontists — surgical specialists in gums and bone; many place implants and manage grafting; some are ABP board-certified.
- Prosthodontists — specialists in restoring teeth and implant-supported prostheses; good to coordinate for the final crown/bridge/denture.
- Implant-trained general dentists — many place implants and manage both surgery and restoration; look for advanced training and a large implant case load.

Credentials and experience to check
- Formal specialty training (oral surgery, periodontics, prosthodontics) or advanced implant training (AAID, ICOI, university residencies, fellowships).
- Board certification where applicable (ABOMS, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics).
- How many implants they place per year and examples of similar cases to yours.
- Experience with grafting/sinus lifts if you need bone augmentation.

Technology and approach
- Use of CBCT (3D imaging) and digital planning for accuracy.
- Guided implant surgery or surgical guides for complex cases.
- In-office lab, digital impressions/scans, and coordination with a prosthodontist when needed.
- Clear treatment plan with timelines, option for temporary tooth (immediate loading) if appropriate.

Practical checks
- Read recent patient reviews (Google, Healthgrades, Yelp, Zocdoc) and look at before/after photos.
- Ask about implant brands used (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer Biomet, etc.) and their warranty policies.
- Ask about sedation options, complication rates, and how they handle problems.
- Cost estimate, what’s included (surgery, implant, abutment, crown), and financing options.

Questions to bring to a consultation
- What are your qualifications and how many implants have you placed?
- Can I see before/after photos of cases like mine?
- Do you use CBCT and digital planning?
- What implant brand do you use and why?
- Will you do the restoration or refer to a prosthodontist?
- What are total costs and payment options?

If you’d like, I can:
- Suggest several well-regarded implant specialists and clinics in Columbus (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood), or
- Help draft a shortlist of questions to email or ask during consults.

Which would you prefer — a list of local providers (tell me your area in Columbus) or help preparing for consultations?
